html:
Piracy off the coast of Somalia grew in the 2000s and peaked between about 2008 and 2011, when Somali pirates seized hundreds of ships in the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean and held their crews for ransom.

With no government after the civil war, foreign trawlers fished Somali waters freely, and local fishermen first armed themselves against them. Gangs based in towns such as Eyl in Puntland then went after merchant ships and oil tankers, earning ransoms in the millions.

Navies from Europe, the United States, China, India and others patrolled the shipping lanes to the Suez Canal, and ships carried armed guards. Attacks fell sharply after 2012. Some revived in the 2020s. The episode showed how the collapse of Somalia reached the world's sea lanes.
sum: Piracy off the coast of Somalia grew in the 2000s and peaked between about 2008 and 2011, when Somali pirates seized hundreds of ships in the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean and held their crews for ransom.
